title: Watch for changes
description:
Write `observe(obj, onChange)` returning a Proxy that reports every change, including changes **inside nested objects and arrays**:

- Setting a property calls `onChange(path, oldValue, newValue)`, where `path` is the property path as an array, such as `["settings", "theme"]` or `["items", "2"]`.
- Setting a property to the value it already has (`Object.is`) calls nothing.
- Deleting a property calls `onChange(path, oldValue, undefined)`.
- Reading a property whose value is an object or array returns an observed version of it, so nested changes are reported with the full path.
- Reading the same nested object twice returns the **same** proxy (keep them in a `WeakMap`).

```javascript
const state = observe({ settings: { theme: "dark" }, items: [] }, (path, from, to) =>
  console.log(path.join("."), from, "->", to));
state.settings.theme = "light";   // settings.theme dark -> light
state.items.push("a");            // items.0 undefined -> a
```
hints: The `get` trap is where nesting happens: when the value read is an object, return `observe(value, onChange, [...path, key])` so its changes carry the longer path.
Pass one `WeakMap` down through every call and look the object up before making a new proxy. `Object.is(old, value)` tells you whether anything really changed.
